 Donald Trump Trump brags about the White House ballroom in his first post-election appearance
 One day after elections in which Democrats took back the House and the Senate, the president addressed workers building the White House ballroom and said he didn’t regret starting the Iran war. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 
 Trump blames Iran war for GOP losses but says he would ‘do it again’ 02:15 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 4, 2026, 1:36 PM EST By Rebecca Shabad In his first public appearance since Republicans racked up major losses in the midterm elections, President Donald Trump boasted Wednesday about the White House ballroom under construction and largely skirted talk about his party’s performance. 
 “This is a special structure. It’s going to be not only one of the biggest, but it’ll be the most beautiful ballroom, I think, anywhere in the world, and they’ve been trying to get it for 150 years,” Trump told construction workers at the ballroom site on the White House grounds, where the East Wing previously stood. 
 “This will be something very special. And so we’re putting up the last piece of steel. I thought it would be appropriate to have the media here,” he added, hinting that the ballroom’s “official opening” would be in the near future. 
 The president’s only remarks on the election results — which saw Democrats regain control of both houses of Congress, notching wins in longtime GOP strongholds like Texas — came in response to questions from the media after his remarks. 
 When asked to weigh in on the race to pick a new House Republican leader in light of Speaker Mike Johnson’s decision not to run again , Trump said, “We’ll stay out of it.” He said he did not ask Johnson to step down.
 Asked for comment on Vice President JD Vance’s statement that Republicans lost the election because of the war on Iran , Trump said, “I think it’s largely true because it drove the gasoline up a little bit short term.” He added: “At the same time, if I had it to do again, I’d have to do it again because long term it’s the only answer. You can’t let Iran have a nuclear weapon.” 
 The president signed a steel beam destined for the ballroom project, adorned with two gold presidential seals, and addressed criticism that he is too focused on White House renovations.

 Slide 1 of 1 Trump claimed that it was “the dream of presidents to have a ballroom for 150 years” and bragged about the “most beautiful marble” in the ballroom. 
 “I got it for the floor of the ballroom at the White House. And it’s going to be beautiful. The walls are going to be very — you’ll see a lot of glass,” he said. 
 Trump first announced plans for the ballroom in July 2025 and has frequently spoken about it during official White House events on unrelated subjects and at campaign rallies. The project has faced legal obstacles, though the Supreme Court said in late August that construction could proceed indefinitely . 
 On Monday, Trump spent most of his final pre-election speech in front of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool touting the renovations he ordered around Washington, D.C., with very little time devoted to the midterms.
